root_cause.text: `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()` in `mm/slub.c` used an incomplete PREEMPT_RT context check that only rejected NMI/hardirq callers, so it could enter `local_lock_irqsave()` from a non-preemptible context where `local_lock` is sleeping and trigger a sleep-in-atomic bug.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq()))` to `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && !preemptible())` and the CVE notes that a BPF tracepoint path with `preempt_count > 0` caused `kmalloc_nolock()` to call `local_lock_irqsave()` and hit “BUG: sleeping function called from invalid context” on PREEMPT_RT.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten the PREEMPT_RT kmalloc_nolock() restriction to fail in all non-preemptible contexts where the allocator cannot safely operate.
intent_record.what: The PREEMPT_RT-specific allocation check in kmalloc_nolock_noprof() was changed from testing in_nmi() || in_hardirq() to testing !preemptible(), and the accompanying comment was expanded to explain that kmalloc_nolock() is unsupported in non-preemptible context because local_lock becomes a sleeping lock on RT.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this causes kmalloc_nolock_noprof() to reject more calling contexts on PREEMPT_RT, returning NULL not only in NMI or hardirq but in any non-preemptible context where sleeping locks cannot be taken safely, preventing invalid allocation attempts in RT-critical sections.

grouping_result.intent: Tighten the PREEMPT_RT kmalloc_nolock() restriction to fail in all non-preemptible contexts where the allocator cannot safely operate.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the same PREEMPT_RT context-check flaw in kmalloc_nolock() by tightening rejection of unsafe non-preemptible callers, which matches the root cause of allowing local_lock_irqsave() from an invalid context and causing sleep-in-atomic issues.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix check only rejected NMI and hardirq callers on PREEMPT_RT, but did not reject other non-preemptible contexts. As a result, kmalloc_nolock_noprof() could still proceed into local_lock_irqsave() from an unsafe context and sleep in atomic context.

vuln_statements.explanation: This PREEMPT_RT guard only excludes NMI and hardirq contexts. It fails to reject other non-preemptible contexts, allowing kmalloc_nolock_noprof() to continue into local_lock_irqsave() and potentially sleep in atomic context.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit af92793e52c3a99b828ed4bdd277fd3e11c18d08
Author: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Date:   Mon Sep 8 18:00:07 2025 -0700

    slab: Introduce kmalloc_nolock() and kfree_nolock().
    
    kmalloc_nolock() relies on ability of local_trylock_t to detect
    the situation when per-cpu kmem_cache is locked.
    
    In !PREEMPT_RT local_(try)lock_irqsave(&s->cpu_slab->lock, flags)
    disables IRQs and marks s->cpu_slab->lock as acquired.
    local_lock_is_locked(&s->cpu_slab->lock) returns
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet already contains the PREEMPT_RT hardirq/NMI guard that prevents the unsafe path described in the root cause. In `kmalloc_nolock_noprof()` it explicitly checks `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq())) return NULL;`, and the later allocation path also avoids entering the risky CPU-slab lock path when spinning is not allowed. In `___slab_alloc()` and `__slab_alloc()`, the code uses `allow_spin = gfpflags_allow_spinning(gfpflags)` and, crucially, before taking the local lock it checks `if (unlikely(!gfpflags_allow_spinning(gfpflags))) { if (local_lock_is_locked(&s->cpu_slab->lock)) { p = ERR_PTR(-EBUSY); goto out; } }`. That means the function no longer blindly enters `local_lock_irqsave()`/`local_lock_cpu_slab()` from a context where the local lock is already held on PREEMPT_RT; it bails out with `-EBUSY` and retries another bucket. So the vulnerable construct is present in the history of the commit, but in this shown version the relevant fix is already implemented, so `has_bug=false` and `is_fixed=true`.
